kitDescription: Alice: Wonderland Bunny is a pure team-support Burst I unit whose personal damage contribution is effectively zero. Every 60 normal attacks she heals the whole team and applies Carrot Party, a stacking buff that raises allies' damage to Interruption Parts (up to 5 stacks, 5 seconds each). When Full Burst ends she speeds up the team's burst gauge refill for 5 seconds, and when Full Burst begins she raises everyone's magazine capacity by 40% for 15 seconds and instantly refills 40% of each ally's magazine. Her burst heals the team and re-opens Burst Stage 1 so a second Burst I unit can also cast in the same rotation; a separate 90-hit line raises Water allies' buff stack caps, and at max Carrot Party stacks her burst would amplify incoming healing — neither of those last two effects is representable in the current engine.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHAs found: all 9 kit lines are either FAITHFUL encodings (7) or verbatim DOCUMENTED_GAPs with sound no-primitive reasoning (2), giving a faithfulness score of 1.0. Convergence is strong and multi-shaped: the S5 blind suite runs 16 PASS / 0 FAIL against the shipped override, the S6 blind override is semantically identical to the driver's (same triggers, targets, stats, values, durations, maxStacks, fraction, stage, effect ordering, and the same unmodeled set), and the driver's own suite carries a discriminating counterfactual for every load-bearing assertion (burst-keyed heal, burst-keyed Carrot Party, fullBurstEnter-keyed gauge buff, self-only max ammo, stripped instantReload, stripped reenterStage, self-only burst heal) — each of which would fail under its named nearest-wrong model, so discriminationOk holds. The S2b vacuity hazard (a Burst-I audited unit never casting beside liter) was independently anticipated and neutralized in both suites via fixtures where she is the casting B1 with positive cast-count assertions. The same-model residual the owner should spot-check is the trio of shared-prior readings every agent landed on identically: (1) 'Reload 40%.' as instantReload fraction 0.4 rather than reloadSpeedPct — structurally justified (no arrow/duration/Speed token) but one recording of the ammo counter at FB entry settles it definitively; (2) hitCount:60 as recurring rather than one-shot — count recovery popups in footage; (3) the capacity-buff-before-refill block ordering (0.4 × 168 vs 0.4 × 120 rounds) — the driver already ⚑-flagged it with a swap recipe. All three are honestly flagged with measurement recipes, none is a fudge, and none blocks GO.
